The main takeaway from our work is that

the Hippo pathway is a major tumor suppressor pathway that is often inactivated in cancer, and that this inactivation is not always due to mutations in the Hippo kinome but also due to mutations in Hippo effectors, such as WWTR1 (TAZ) and YAP.

the fusion of two proteins that are normally antagonists (TAZ and CAMTA1) leads to constitutive TAZ activation and oncogenic transformation, and that this mechanism of activation may be relevant to other TAZ fusions.
